intent: A tropical question with a northern answer: three island bars that dwarf the tropics, a counter that runs to 267,000, a pin on the capital built across 14 islands, and a rocky-skerry close that explains why nobody lives on most of them.
pacing_profile: question read verbatim, three options, 3-s beat, reveal with the number, story beats shaped per episode (brief.md), punchline + short follow
pause_policy: Pause only at the marked ellipses; the beat is real silence (ticks come from quizscore.py).
title: Which country has the MOST islands?

lines.direction: the question, cold — curiosity comes from the map moving under it
lines.text: Which country has the most islands?

lines.direction: quick, each option its own beat

lines.text: Sweden. Its statistics office counts about 267,000 islands, more than anyone else.

lines.direction: ease back over the Baltic; three island bars rise on 'Indonesia' with Sweden off the chart; the Indonesian flag-ball thinks on 'Philippines'; a plus sticker on 'together' as Sweden pulses
lines.text: Indonesia has around 17,000. The Philippines, 7,600. Sweden beats both together.

lines.direction: tighten on Stockholm; the inhabited counter runs 0 → 1,000 on 'living' with a house sticker; the Stockholm pin and 14-islands tag on 'capital'; a crown sticker on '14' as Sweden pulses; the pin leaves at the end
lines.text: Only about 1,000 of them have anyone living there. The capital alone sits on 14 islands.

lines.direction: drift north up the Gulf of Bothnia; a rock sticker on 'skerries'; the RISING LAND card and the Bothnia tag on 'ice'; a sparkle sticker on 'new' as the Swedish flag-ball grins and Sweden pulses
lines.text: Most are skerries, bare rock lifted by land still rising since the ice age. New islands appear every year.

lines.direction: punchline, then a short follow — the outro visual asks
lines.text: All those islands, 1 country. Follow us.
